docs.title: amplifactory
docs.text:
amplifactory turns a repository into an issue-driven agent factory. You and Claude (Opus) turn an idea into prioritized lanes of ordered GitHub issues. Then the factory takes each issue from plan to merged pull request: a Sonnet builder plans, builds and fixes, a fresh Opus reviewer checks the work, and Opus merges when every gate passes. When it needs a decision from you, it asks on the pull request and keeps working on other lanes.

It's a Copier template: one command creates a repo with the rules, the skill, CI, labels, branch protection and a Project board. copier update brings later releases into existing projects.

idea ──► brainstorm with Opus ──► lanes (P0–P3) of ordered issues ──► you confirm once
                                                                          │
         ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         ▼   per lane, one issue at a time, in order
   Sonnet builder: plan ──► (Opus checks the plan) ──► build ──► PR
                                                                  │
   fresh Opus reviewer ∥ CI ──► builder fixes blockers ──► gates ──► merge
         │
         └─ needs you? question inline on the PR, lane paused, other lanes continue

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
• Create a project

    Generate a repo from the template, then run bootstrap.sh for the GitHub side: labels, branch protection and the Project board.

    Create a project

  • Your first run

    Brainstorm into lanes, then say "run the factory" and watch the first issue go from plan to merge.

    Your first run

docs.title: What makes it work
docs.text: Idea In short Lanes and priorities Features become lanes, each a parent issue whose native sub-issues run in order. P0–P3 priorities and "blocked by" links drive the schedule. One lane at a time unless you say otherwise. The pipeline Two subagents per issue: one Sonnet builder reused for plan, build and fixes, and one fresh Opus reviewer. Only blockers are fixed in-PR before a first release; everything else becomes an improvement issue. Flag and continue Questions go on the PR as inline comments with options and a recommendation. You answer whenever you like, then say "resume". Proposals become issues Follow-ups and audit results the orchestrator proposes are proposed as a sub-issue, lane or doc-debt issue, never as an ad-hoc fix. One confirmation creates it. Where knowledge lives GitHub and the repo are the source of truth: issues, PRs, review threads, plans, Handoffs. The run log and Claude's memory only point at them.

docs.title: Where it came from
docs.text: The factory started as a label-by-label GitHub Actions pipeline for one project. It was then generalized into this template and hardened by driving a real project, pensieve-traces, through it. Every factory problem found along the way became a lesson issue and then a release. The changelog tells that story, one release at a time.

docs.title: The GitHub Actions mode
docs.text:
Every generated repo also contains the Actions mode: agents that run on GitHub's servers when you add labels. It's slower than the skill but needs nothing running on your machine.

issue ──(you: factory:design)──► DESIGN agent ──► draft design PR
                                                      │  you review; "@claude revise …"
                              (you: design:approved) ─┘
                                                      ▼
                     BUILD agent on factory/issue-N: implement, run checks until green, open PR
                                                      ▼
                     REVIEW agent: PR vs. approved design + CLAUDE.md
                                                      ▼
                                              you merge
Workflow Runs when factory-design.yml you add factory:design to an issue factory-build.yml you add design:approved to a design PR factory-review.yml a build PR opens or updates factory-chat.yml you write @claude on an issue or PR factory-label-guard.yml anyone but you adds a trigger label: it's removed

docs.title: GitHub quirks it works around
docs.text:
• A PR that changes a workflow skips that workflow's stage. Workflow changes go in their own PR.
  • PR runs use the merge ref from when the PR was last updated. After a merge, click Update branch on open PRs, or they run old workflows.
  • PRs authored by claude[bot] need allowed_bots and the right restrict_untrusted_prs setting, or the review job is green but does nothing.

docs.title: Using both
docs.text: The skill and the Actions mode share .claude/commands/ and CLAUDE.md. The skill never adds trigger labels or writes @claude, so the two don't start each other. Pick one per issue.

docs.title: Flag and continue
docs.text: The factory never stops the run to wait for you, unless nothing else can proceed.

docs.title: When it asks
docs.text:
• A plan or review raises a question only you can answer (scope, an interface, a dependency, a data source).
  • A gate fails and the fix isn't mechanical.
  • The orchestrator is unsure whether to merge (gate 12).
  • More lanes are ready than you've allowed (asked once, in the session).

docs.title: How it asks
docs.text:
1. An inline review comment on the exact line, tagged [question], with options and a recommendation.
  2. The label factory:needs-maintainer on the PR.
  3. The run log records it as asked, with a link to the thread.
  4. Only that lane pauses. Other lanes, and anything that doesn't depend on this issue, carry on.

docs.title: How you answer
docs.text:
Reply in the thread on GitHub, whenever you like: from your phone, the next day, in a different session. Then, in Claude Code:

resume the factory

queue.py detects your reply after the question and lists that lane as replied, ahead of new work. The orchestrator reads your answer, applies it (via the builder), resolves the thread, removes the label and continues to the gates.

docs.title: Ready to merge
docs.text:
A refused merge is not a question, so it isn't factory:needs-maintainer. When every gate passes but the merge is refused (the harness denies gh pr merge, or GitHub rejects it), the factory:

  1. labels the PR and issue factory:ready-to-merge and removes the in-progress label;
  2. posts one PR comment: the exact merge command and the gate summary;
  3. moves on. The issue stays open, so its lane's later issues wait.

It never works around the refusal. queue.py lists these under "Waiting for you to merge", and the end-of-run report lists them so you can merge in one batch.

Opt in to merging itself. You can add a permission rule to the repo's .claude/settings.json or your user ~/.claude/settings.json:

{ "permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(gh pr merge * --merge --admin --delete-branch)"] } }

The syntax follows the Claude Code permissions docs. The rule lets the agent use your ruleset bypass, so it is your choice and the template doesn't ship it. The rule matches only commands that end in --delete-branch, which is how the skill runs the merge (gates.md "Merge"); variants with -R or other trailing flags aren't covered. A project rule applies only after you accept the workspace trust prompt. How allow rules interact with auto mode is described in the permission modes docs; check it, and try it in your own session.

docs.title: What never happens
docs.text:
• The skill never adds the Actions-mode trigger labels (factory:design, design:approved) and never writes @claude. Those would start GitHub Actions agents.
  • PRs that change .github/, CLAUDE.md or .claude/ are never merged by the factory. You merge those.

docs.title: Lanes and priorities
docs.text:
A lane is a feature or swim lane: something one builder could carry from start to finish. On GitHub it's a parent issue labelled lane, and its native sub-issues, in order, are the lane's issues.

Lane A: STS end-to-end (P0)      #4 ──► #6
Lane B: ConvoMem datasets (P1)   #5 ──► #8 ──► #9
Lane C: OpenRouter traces (P2)   #7
Lane D: Hardening (P3)           #17 ──► #18 ──► … ──► #25     (blocked by lane A)

docs.title: The rules
docs.text: Rule Within a lane Strictly in order, one issue at a time. The current issue is the first open sub-issue. When it merges, the next one becomes current. Across lanes Ranked by priority. One lane at a time by default. When more lanes are ready, the skill asks you once whether to run them in parallel. Priority Exactly one label: P0 must have now, P1 next, P2 later, P3 someday or hardening. A missing label counts as P2. Dependencies Native "blocked by" links, between issues or whole lanes. The body's "Depends on #N" line is still read as a fallback. Questions A question on a lane's PR pauses only that lane. A paused lane uses no slot, so the next lane may start. Merges Always one at a time, whatever the number of lanes.

docs.title: The main path
docs.text: Every brainstorm names a main path: the smallest chain of issues that makes the thing work end to end. It's a P0 lane. Polish and hardening go in a low-priority lane, so the factory doesn't spend its effort perfecting a parser before anything consumes its output.

docs.title: Rolling-wave detail
docs.text: Only the next one or two issues per lane are written in full. Later ones are stubs (a title, one-line goal and dependencies) and get detailed when they come close. Plans written too early go stale.

docs.title: Parallel lanes
docs.text: If you allow --lanes N, up to N lanes are active at once, each with its own worktree and builder. Before a second lane starts, a collision guard compares its plan's "Files & interfaces touched" with the files the other active lane is changing, and holds it if they overlap. After each merge, the other active lanes' branches are updated with main before their review.

docs.title: Proposals become issues
docs.text: Work the orchestrator proposes becomes issues, not an ad-hoc fix. This covers what the run's own routes don't: audit results, recommended follow-ups, and fixes it would offer at the end of a turn or in the final report. It proposes a sub-issue of the lane that fits, a new lane if none does, or a doc-debt sub-issue, naming the lane, title and priority. One confirmation creates them with gh issue create, wired with lanes.py, and the work then goes through the queue. Findings inside a run keep their routes (improvement issues, doc-debt, PR questions). Problems in the factory template repo are lesson issues (the factory-lesson skill).

docs.title: Seeing it
docs.text:
• python .claude/skills/factory/scripts/queue.py prints the lanes, each lane's current issue and state (active, replied, ready, asked, blocked, waiting, done), and "Work now".
  • The Project board created by bootstrap.sh: group by Parent issue to see each lane with a progress bar, and sort by Priority.
  • scripts/lanes.py creates and reorders lanes, sub-issues, dependencies and priorities.

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
The skill runs in your Claude Code session. You (Opus) are the orchestrator: you pick the work, check plans, verify findings and merge. The heavy lifting goes to two subagents per issue.

Role Model Lifetime Does Orchestrator Opus (your session) the run queue, plan check, gates, merge, run log Builder Sonnet one per issue, reused via SendMessage plan → build → fixes, keeps the PR's Handoff current Design reviewer Opus, fresh critical issues only reviews the plan before any code Code reviewer Opus, fresh once per issue inline findings while CI runs

docs.title: One issue, step by step
docs.text:
1. Plan. The builder writes .factory/designs/issue-N.md (goal, approach, files and interfaces touched, dependencies, risks, tests) and opens a draft PR from local/issue-N.
  2. Plan check. Standard issues: you read the plan. Critical issues (privacy or security code, a new dependency, a shared data contract, a public interface others build on) get a fresh Opus design reviewer.
  3. Build. The same builder implements, updates the docs the change affects, runs the checks from CLAUDE.md until green, fills in the PR's Handoff (including a Docs line: what was updated, or "none needed" and why) and marks it ready.
  4. Review ∥ CI. A fresh Opus reviewer reads the diff against the plan and CLAUDE.md and posts inline comments tagged [blocker], [improvement], [doc-debt] or [question]. Every blocker comes with a reproduction. It also checks that docs and code agree in the changed area (see Docs ship with the code).
  5. Fix. The builder fixes blockers. You verify each with its reproduction on the new commit and resolve the thread. There is no second full review.
  6. Gates and merge. When all thirteen gates pass, the factory merges (merge commit) and the lane moves on. If the merge is refused, it hands the PR to you instead (see Ready to merge).

docs.title: Real data
docs.text: CLAUDE.md has a Real data line: never (the default), with-approval or allowed. The skill reads it from main; a missing or unrecognised line means never. Under with-approval, the maintainer approves one named source on the issue or PR, for that issue or PR only. At every level, real data is never committed or quoted (shapes only) and tests use synthetic fixtures.

docs.title: Urgency triage
docs.text:
CLAUDE.md has a Release phase line. In mvp (until a first formal release), only blockers are fixed in a PR:

  • the main path breaks on realistic input;
  • private data leaks on realistic input;
  • a hard rule is violated;
  • irreversible loss or overwrite of the user's existing data (source files, history, remote repos) on a plausible invocation, even a mistaken one, when a cheap guard would prevent it;
  • a test falsely passes.

Everything else is collected into one improvement issue per PR, usually in a hardening lane. Switch the line to hardening before a release, and reviews become thorough again.

docs.title: Docs ship with the code
docs.text:
A CLAUDE.md hard rule: every code change brings its documentation in the same PR, both new docs for new behaviour and updates to any README, CHANGELOG, docstring or .factory/designs/ text it makes wrong or stale.

  • A PR whose docs disagree with its code breaks a hard rule, so it's a blocker, even in mvp.
  • A mismatch that was already there before the PR is tagged [doc-debt] and isn't fixed in that PR. The orchestrator files it as a sub-issue of the repo's "Documentation tech-debt" issue (labels documentation, P2; each todo documentation, improvement, P2) with lanes.py doc-debt add.
  • Ride-alongs: the builder is given the open todos. When its PR already touches a file one of them is about, it fixes that too and the PR closes it.
  • Documentation todos that come up while planning also go under the tracking issue.

bootstrap.sh creates the tracking issue; in older repos the skill creates it the first time it's needed (lanes.py doc-debt find). This came from pensieve-traces, whose README still called a built feature "planned".

docs.title: Why this shape
docs.text: The first version used cold subagents for every stage, re-reviewed after every fix and treated every finding as a blocker. Two issues cost about 1.4M subagent tokens. Reusing one builder, using one fresh reviewer and triaging by urgency cut most of that, without losing the defects that matter. Opus reviews reproduced bugs, including privacy leaks, that an earlier Sonnet review had called "ready".

docs.title: Where knowledge lives
docs.text: Place Holds Who reads it Issues goals, acceptance criteria, lane structure, priorities, dependencies everyone PRs the diff, the Handoff, review threads, questions and answers everyone .factory/designs/issue-N.md the plan, shipped inside the PR reviewers, future agents CLAUDE.md project context, release phase, real-data access, checks, hard rules every agent, every session lesson issues in amplifactory factory problems found while driving a project the template's next release .factory/runs/ (gitignored) run log: events, timings, token costs, pointers to PRs, commits and threads the orchestrator, for resume and cost Claude's memory (~/.claude/projects/…) your preferences, how you like to work your Claude sessions on this machine

docs.title: The run log only points
docs.text: The run log never holds a decision. It says things like "PR #34 asked a question, thread …" or "issue #4 merged at e24eea1, 410k tokens". If the run log is deleted, nothing is lost but the cost history: the state can be rebuilt from GitHub.

docs.title: The Handoff
docs.text:
Every PR body has a ## Handoff section, kept current by the builder after every change:

  • what changed and why;
  • key decisions;
  • how to test;
  • what's open.

A fresh session, a fresh reviewer or you start from it, instead of from a transcript.

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text: You need uv, git, the GitHub CLI (gh, logged in) and Claude Code.

docs.title: 1. Generate the repo
docs.text:
uvx copier copy gh:rahmansunny071/amplifactory my-project

Copier asks a few questions: the project and package names, a description, what the agents should know about the project, project-specific hard rules, Python versions, the release phase and whether agents may read your real data (never by default). Defaults are filled in.

Private template

If the template repo is private, Copier needs your GitHub credentials. Run gh auth setup-git so the gh: shortcut (HTTPS) uses your gh login, or use git@github.com:rahmansunny071/amplifactory.git.

docs.title: 2. Give gh the scopes it needs
docs.text:
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s repo,workflow,project
  • workflow: creating a repo that contains GitHub Actions workflows.
  • project: the factory's Project board.

docs.title: 3. Run the bootstrap
docs.text:
cd my-project
./scripts/bootstrap.sh --public      # or --private

bootstrap.sh does what a template can't. It's safe to re-run:

Step What it does Lockfile and first commit uv lock, then git init and the first commit GitHub repo creates and pushes it (--public or --private) Labels the factory labels, improvement, lane, P0–P3 and documentation Documentation tech-debt issue the tracking issue whose sub-issues are documentation todos (labels documentation, P2) Ruleset protecting main no deletion or force push; PRs need 1 approval and code-owner review; all conversations resolved; required checks Tests (Python X) and Lint; admins can bypass for PRs only Fork PRs workflows from outside contributors need your approval Project board "<project> factory", linked to the repo, with a Priority field

Rulesets need a public repo or GitHub Pro

On GitHub Free, rulesets aren't enforced on private repos. Then main isn't protected, and the script says so.

docs.title: 4. Optional: the GitHub Actions mode
docs.text:
The Actions mode runs agents on GitHub's servers when you add labels. It needs the Claude GitHub App and a token secret:

  1. In Claude Code, run /install-github-app, pick the repo, and choose your subscription. That saves CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
  2. Close the PR the installer opens (claude.yml, claude-code-review.yml). The template's factory-chat.yml and factory-review.yml already cover those, with sender and fork checks.

The factory skill doesn't need any of this. It runs in your Claude Code session.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Your first run →

docs.title: Your first run
docs.text:
Start Claude Code from inside the repo so it loads the repo's CLAUDE.md and the factory skill, and check that it's on Opus:

cd my-project
claude          # then /model to confirm Opus

docs.title: 1. Brainstorm into lanes
docs.text:
brainstorm a CLI that converts session logs into a dataset into issues

Opus talks it through with you: goals, constraints, what's out of scope, and how you'll know it works. Then it proposes lanes: features with a priority (P0–P3) and dependencies between them. Inside each lane are the ordered issues. Only the next one or two per lane are written in full; the rest are stubs. You'll see a table like this:

Lane Priority Issues, in order Depends on A: core conversion P0 reader → writer + CLI — B: dataset builder P1 export → builder → validation — C: hardening P3 edge cases… lane A

Confirm once. It creates the lane issues, their sub-issues in order, the "blocked by" links, the priority labels and the Project board items. See Lanes and priorities.

docs.title: 2. Run the factory
docs.text:
run the factory

  1. queue.py shows each lane's current issue and "Work now". If several lanes are ready, it asks you whether to run them in parallel. The default is one lane.
  2. A Sonnet builder writes the plan (.factory/designs/issue-N.md) and opens a draft PR from a local/issue-N branch.
  3. Opus checks the plan. For a critical issue (privacy or security code, a new dependency, a shared data contract), a fresh Opus design reviewer does it.
  4. The same builder builds, updates the docs the change affects, fills in the PR's Handoff (with its Docs line), and marks the PR ready.
  5. A fresh Opus reviewer posts inline comments tagged [blocker], [improvement], [doc-debt] or [question], while CI runs. Docs that disagree with the PR's code are a blocker.
  6. The builder fixes blockers. Improvements become one improvement issue; doc-debt findings become sub-issues of the "Documentation tech-debt" issue.
  7. When every gate passes, including all review threads resolved, Opus merges. The lane moves to its next issue. If the merge is refused, the PR is labelled factory:ready-to-merge with the merge command in a comment, and you merge it (details).

docs.title: 3. When it needs you
docs.text:
You'll see a question on the PR with options and a recommendation, and the label factory:needs-maintainer. Only that lane pauses. Reply in the thread whenever it suits you, then:

resume the factory

See Flag and continue.

docs.title: 4. At the end
docs.text: The run summary lists what was merged, what's waiting on you, which improvements were filed, and the time and token cost per issue (scripts/runlog.py summary). Start a fresh session every two or three issues: GitHub and the run log let it pick up where the last one stopped.

docs.title: Option 1: the whole template
docs.text:
Run Copier into the existing repo. It asks the same questions and shows a conflict for every file that already exists:

cd existing-repo
uvx copier copy gh:rahmansunny071/amplifactory .

Keep your own pyproject.toml, package and tests where they conflict. Take CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .factory/, .github/ and scripts/bootstrap.sh from the template, then merge your existing CI into ci.yml and the "checks pass" list in CLAUDE.md, which must stay identical. Run ./scripts/bootstrap.sh: it skips what already exists.

Because .copier-answers.yml now exists, later releases come in with uvx copier update.

docs.title: Option 2: just the skill
docs.text:
If you only want the Claude Code skill:

URL=https://github.com/rahmansunny071/amplifactory.git; TAG=vX.Y.Z   # a release tag
T=$(mktemp -d)                                  # outside the repo
git init -q --bare "$T/src"
git -C "$T/src" fetch -q --depth 1 "$URL" "refs/tags/${TAG}:refs/tags/${TAG}"
test "$(git -C "$T/src" cat-file -t "refs/tags/$TAG")" = tag || { echo "not annotated: stop"; false; }  # must be tag
git -C "$T/src" archive "$TAG" template/.claude/skills | tar -x -k --strip-components=2 -C .claude/

Use a release tag, never main: the skill itself refuses anything else. Releases up to v0.7.0 have no sync-root-factory folder, so use the first release that ships it. tar -k keeps files you already have, so a skill of the same name is not overwritten (check .claude/skills/ for one). Commit the result. This is for a repo that has no factory skill yet; if you already have factory/, follow Keeping the skill up to date instead.

Then add to your CLAUDE.md:

  • a Release phase line (mvp or hardening) and the blocker definition;
  • a Real data section whose first line is Real data: never. (or with-approval / allowed); without it the skill treats the repo as never;
  • a "checks pass" list identical to your CI;
  • the hard rules you want enforced (see the template's CLAUDE.md.jinja), including "every code change ships its docs in the same PR";
  • Where knowledge lives.

And create the labels the skill uses: factory:needs-maintainer, factory:ready-to-merge, improvement, lane, P0–P3, documentation. The skill creates the "Documentation tech-debt" issue itself the first time it needs it.

docs.title: Keeping the skill up to date
docs.text:
.claude/skills/factory/VERSION (written by the sync, and shipped from the first release that has it) records which release the copy came from. Then, in Claude Code in the repo:

sync the factory to the latest release

The sync-root-factory skill:

  • works on a new branch local/adopt-<tag> cut from a fresh origin/<default branch>, and refuses a dirty tree;
  • replaces every skill folder the tag ships (factory/, factory-lesson/, sync-root-factory/ and any future one) byte for byte from the tag. A folder the old tag had is replaced only after it matches the version the repo claims; a new one is added; a folder the old tag did not have but you already have (your own skill, or a hand copy) is refused, never overwritten; your own other skills are never touched;
  • turns the CHANGELOG entries since your version into a checklist; it edits CLAUDE.md, .claude/commands/*, README.md and CHANGELOG.md for the ports it can do safely, never sets a policy value (the Real data: level, the release phase), creates only the labels that are missing, and lists everything else under "Open";
  • opens a PR with a Handoff and never merges it.

Every sync, the first included: run the target tag's sync.py, extracted outside the repo, never the copy in the repo (which may predate the guards, and does not exist yet the first time). Nothing is committed before the adopt branch exists, so this works on a protected main:

R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); URL=https://github.com/rahmansunny071/amplifactory.git; TAG=vX.Y.Z  # latest release
T=$(mktemp -d)                                  # outside the repo
git init -q --bare "$T/src"
git -C "$T/src" fetch -q --depth 1 "$URL" "refs/tags/${TAG}:refs/tags/${TAG}"
git -C "$T/src" cat-file -t "refs/tags/$TAG"    # must print: tag  (annotated)
mkdir "$T/x" && git -C "$T/src" archive "$TAG" template/.claude/skills/sync-root-factory | tar -x -C "$T/x"
python3 -I "$T/x/template/.claude/skills/sync-root-factory/scripts/sync.py" --repo "$R" status --assume-tag v0.7.0

--assume-tag is needed only while factory/VERSION is missing (the first sync): it stands in for the file, and the folder is still checked against that tag. Then ask Claude to sync; the skill runs the same extracted script. The old way (copy sync-root-factory/ into the repo and commit it) is no longer needed: the adopt branch is cut from origin/<default>, which would not contain that commit. If you already committed one and the old tag did not ship it (before v0.8.0), apply refuses it; on local/adopt-<tag> run git rm -r .claude/skills/sync-root-factory, commit, and rerun.

If the check fails (your copy matches no tag, for example because a main-only commit was layered on a tag): the sync stops and lists the differing files. There is no override. If the edits are unwanted, restore the copy of the recorded tag, the one verify-local compared against (the version in factory/VERSION, or your --assume-tag; not the target tag, whose VERSION would make the repo look synced). Do it on local/adopt-<target tag>, because a commit on local main is not on the adopt branch:

OLD=v0.7.0                                      # the recorded tag
git init -q --bare "$T/old"
git -C "$T/old" fetch -q --depth 1 "$URL" "refs/tags/${OLD}:refs/tags/${OLD}"
test "$(git -C "$T/old" cat-file -t "refs/tags/$OLD")" = tag || { echo "not annotated: stop"; false; }
rm -rf "$R/.claude/skills/factory"
git -C "$T/old" archive "$OLD" template/.claude/skills/factory | tar -x --strip-components=2 -C "$R/.claude/"
git -C "$R" add -A .claude/skills/factory && git -C "$R" commit -m "restore factory/ to $OLD"

then rerun the sync. If the edits are wanted, port them after the sync.

A repo generated by Copier doesn't need any of this: it records its version in .copier-answers.yml, and the sync runs copier update, after sync.py copier-check <tag> confirms the tag is annotated, _commit is a release tag and _src_path is the GitHub template (not a local clone).

Renamed from agent-factory

The template was renamed to amplifactory. A repo whose .copier-answers.yml still says _src_path: gh:rahmansunny071/agent-factory keeps working (GitHub redirects the old URL and copier-check accepts both names). Updating that line to gh:rahmansunny071/amplifactory is optional.

docs.title: Organise existing issues into lanes
docs.text:
organise the open issues into lanes

Opus proposes lanes, an order and priorities; after your confirmation it wires them with lanes.py. That's how pensieve-traces moved to lanes: four lanes, thirteen issues, four "blocked by" links.

docs.title: Day-to-day
docs.text:
Always start Claude Code from the repo's folder, on Opus.

You say What happens "brainstorm X into issues" Two-level brainstorm: lanes, then ordered issues. You confirm once; everything is created and wired. "run the factory" queue.py picks the work; issues go plan → build → review → merge, lane by lane. "run lanes A and B in parallel" Raises the lane limit for this run (otherwise it asks when more lanes are ready). "resume the factory" Picks up replied questions first, then in-flight issues from the run log, then new work. "what's the factory doing?" queue.py plus runlog.py status: lanes, current issues, what's waiting on you. "how much did that cost?" runlog.py summary: wall time, fix rounds and tokens by model, per issue. "move #9 before #8" lanes.py order, then the lane runs in the new order.

docs.title: On GitHub
docs.text:
• Answer questions in PR threads labelled factory:needs-maintainer, then say "resume".
  • Merge PRs the factory won't: anything touching .github/, CLAUDE.md or .claude/.
  • Triage improvement issues when a lane finishes: give them a priority, add them to a hardening lane, or close them.
  • Glance at the Project board, grouped by Parent issue.

docs.title: Keeping sessions small
docs.text: Start a fresh session every two or three issues. Nothing lives only in the session: GitHub has the work, the run log has the pointers and costs, and "resume the factory" rebuilds the picture.

docs.title: Before a release
docs.text: Change CLAUDE.md's Release phase to hardening (in its own PR, which you merge). Reviews become thorough, and improvements are fixed in-PR instead of filed.

docs.title: Evolving the template
docs.text: The factory is tested by real use. A project driven through it is the proving ground; what goes wrong becomes template changes.

docs.title: 1. File a lesson
docs.text:
A factory problem (not a bug in the project's own code) found while driving a project is filed in amplifactory as an issue labelled lesson:

  • what happened, with links;
  • the fix applied in the project, if any;
  • the template files to change.

File it when it happens, not at the end of the run.

In a generated repo, ask Claude Code to "file a factory lesson: ..." and the factory-lesson skill does it:

  1. finds the template repo from .copier-answers.yml (_src_path), used only when it is a GitHub source (gh:, https://github.com/, ssh://git@github.com/, git@github.com:); a local path, an empty value or a missing file falls back to rahmansunny071/amplifactory; the old slug rahmansunny071/agent-factory (any case) is mapped to the new one; it then confirms the slug with gh repo view and confirms it with gh repo view; it never files in the current repo;
  2. searches open and closed lesson issues for a duplicate: an open match gets a comment instead of a new issue; a closed match means it is already fixed, so it points to the release that fixed it and to updating (copier update, or the sync-root-factory skill);
  3. drafts the body (What happened, Fix applied in the generated repo, Template files to change, Options, Takeaway) and checks it for real data values, secrets and private paths, since the issue goes to another repo;
  4. asks you once (if you edit the draft, it re-checks the edited text for real data and shows the result before filing), then creates it with the lesson label and reports the URL;
  5. offers a comment on the downstream PR or issue linking the lesson, only if you agree.

It needs a gh login with access to the template repo (private repos need one).

docs.title: 2. Release
docs.text:
Lessons are batched into a release:

  1. a branch release/vX.Y.Z and a PR that closes the lessons;
  2. a CHANGELOG.md entry saying what changed and why, and template/.claude/skills/factory/VERSION set to X.Y.Z. Rename the Unreleased entry to vX.Y.Z (date) in the same commit as the bump; template CI's version job compares VERSION with the first - vX.Y.Z bullet, so a forgotten bump fails the PR;
  3. template CI green: it renders three variants, runs each generated project's checks, and asserts every guardrail is present;
  4. you merge, then tag vX.Y.Z. Copier only sees tags.

docs.title: 3. Update projects
docs.text:
cd my-project && uvx copier update

Copier does a three-way merge and marks conflicts. Or, in Claude Code inside the project, say "sync the factory to the latest release": the sync-root-factory skill does it on a local/adopt-<tag> branch and opens a PR (mechanical conflicts resolved, the rest listed for you; it never merges). It also works for a project that only carries the skill: it replaces every skill folder the tag ships (factory/, factory-lesson/, sync-root-factory/) from the tag after checking each matches the version it claims (a new one is added; a local one the old tag lacked is refused), using the target tag's sync.py extracted outside the repo, and builds a hand-port checklist from the CHANGELOG entries. See Adopt in an existing repo for the first-time setup.

docs.title: Developing the template
docs.text:
• Template files live in template/; files ending in .jinja are rendered.
  • Copier variables use [[ … ]] and blocks [% … %], so GitHub Actions expressions (${{ … }}) stay untouched.
  • The guardrail check also scans rendered files for leftover template syntax. Python code must avoid sequences that look like it, such as two closing square brackets in a row; use type aliases.
  • To render the working tree instead of the latest tag, use --vcs-ref HEAD.
  • This site is built from docs/ with MkDocs Material. The changelog page is generated from CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
• Unreleased: Renamed to amplifactory (#67): the repo is rahmansunny071/amplifactory; the name changes in URLs, prose and generated text.
  • #67: rename agent-factory to amplifactory. sync.py accepts the old and new names (gh, https, ssh) as the official _src_path, still refuses local clones and forks, and is_template_repo detects the template repo under either name; factory-lesson files into the new repo when the answers file names the old one; site_url, repo_url and repo_name follow. The skill folder names stay. Existing repos may update _src_path (optional; GitHub redirects the old URL).
  • v0.12.0 (2026-11-25): Skill scripts run on Python 3.9; lanes.py reads every page (#63): macOS's system python3 works, template CI runs every self-test under 3.9, and lanes with more than 30 sub-issues work.
  • #63: pagination, fallback test, Python 3.9. lanes.py reads every page of a lane's sub-issues (gh api --paginate), so sub-add/order work in lanes of more than 30. --self-test now covers sub-add's order fallback (a fake whose POST prepends) and a multi-page lane. Every skill script runs on Python 3.9 (lanes.py used itertools.pairwise); Template CI runs all four self-tests under 3.9 as well, and the docs state 3.9 as the minimum. The sub-add line in the factory SKILL.md is rewrapped.
  • v0.11.0 (2026-11-25): lanes.py sub-add appends (#60): adding an issue to a lane no longer jumps it ahead of the lane's next step.
  • #60: lanes.py sub-add appends. It used to put the newly added issues first in the lane (via order); it now keeps the lane's order and puts new issues last, in the order given. Issues already in the lane stay put. order is still how to move issues to the front. --self-test covers it with a fake _gh that models GitHub.
  • v0.10.0 (2026-11-25): Proposals become issues (#56): work the orchestrator offers outside a run's own routes is proposed as issues, sub-issues or lanes, not as an ad-hoc fix.
  • #56: proposals become issues. The factory skill gains a fifth principle: work the orchestrator proposes beyond a run's own routes (audit results, recommended follow-ups, fixes it would offer) is proposed as a sub-issue, lane or doc-debt issue (created with gh issue create, wired with lanes.py) instead of an ad-hoc fix, and "When you're done" reports follow-ups that way.
  • v0.9.0 (2026-11-25): sync-root-factory hardened by its first real run (#50, #48): every sync runs the release tag's own sync.py, apply syncs every skill folder the tag ships (your own skills are never touched), and generated repos get a copier-check before copier update. Plus factory-lesson follow-ups (#47).
  • #50: sync-root-factory gaps from the first real run (pensieve-traces v0.6.0 to v0.8.0).
    • Bootstrap fits a protected main: extract the release tag's sync-root-factory/ into a temp dir outside the repo (depth-1 fetch of the annotated tag, git archive) and run its sync.py --repo <repo root>. Nothing is committed before the adopt branch exists. This replaces v0.8.0's "copy, commit, run" (see "Adopt in an existing repo"). Every sync, not only the first, now runs the target tag's script, so a repo whose in-repo sync.py predates a fix still gets it.
    • apply syncs every skill folder the tag ships under template/.claude/skills/ (so factory-lesson/ and future skills arrive), not a fixed pair. Old-tag folders are replaced only after verify-local; new folders are added; a folder the old tag lacked but you already have (tracked, untracked, gitignored, a symlink, a case-variant name, even a byte-identical hand copy) is refused with the way out (rename it, or git rm -r it on the adopt branch, commit, rerun); a folder the tag dropped is left alone and listed; your own skills are never touched. Every check for every folder runs before the first write. A repo that hand-copied factory-lesson/ (tracked, from a tag that shipped it) syncs normally; one that added it from a tag that did not must remove it first.
    • labels is never silent: it prints none missing (plus any skipped Actions-only labels) when there is nothing to create.
  • #48: copier-check. sync.py copier-check <tag> runs before copier update in a generated repo: the tag must be annotated, _commit a vX.Y.Z tag, and _src_path the GitHub template (gh:rahmansunny071/agent-factory or its https/ssh URL; a local clone or a fork is refused with the fix: edit the existing line, commit, rerun; a repeated _src_path or _commit line is refused, since Copier keeps the last one). status reports src_ok.
  • v0.8.0 (2026-11-25): Two new skills in every generated repo: sync-root-factory (#40) brings a repo up to the latest agent-factory release, and factory-lesson (#41) files a factory problem as a lesson issue here. Plus queue follow-ups (#42).
  • factory-lesson skill (#41). Ships in every generated repo (.claude/skills/factory-lesson/). "File a factory lesson: ..." files a lesson issue in the template repo instead of by hand: it reads the template slug from .copier-answers.yml _src_path (only a GitHub source counts; anything else, such as a local path, uses the default rahmansunny071/agent-factory; confirmed with gh repo view; never the current repo), searches open lessons for a duplicate and offers to comment there, drafts the lesson format (What happened, Fix applied, Template files to change, Options, Takeaway), checks the draft against the Real data rules (no data values, secrets or private paths), asks for one confirmation, creates it with the lesson label, and offers a back-link comment. No lessons lane or board. The factory skill's "When you're done" now points to it. Template CI guards the skill file.
  • #40: sync-root-factory skill, shipped in every generated repo: it brings a repo up to the latest release tag in one step and hands the result over as a PR. Say "sync the factory to the latest release" in Claude Code.
    • scripts/sync.py enforces the guards (new branch local/adopt-<tag> from a fresh origin/<default>, clean tree, never inside agent-factory, files only from the annotated release tag, verify-local before any overwrite, symlinked or out-of-repo target folders refused, only tracked files replaced, only missing labels created, push of that one branch); the agent does the judgement. Every refusal happens before a write, except apply's post-check, which says how to undo.
    • Generated repos: copier update --vcs-ref <tag> --defaults --conflict inline; mechanical conflicts only, the rest goes to the PR's Open section; conflict markers and .rej files are never committed.
    • Shadowing repos (copy the skill by hand): replaces .claude/skills/factory/ byte for byte after checking it matches the version it claims, builds a hand-port checklist from the CHANGELOG entries, never applies a policy value (such as the Real data: level). A folder that matches no tag stops the sync and lists the differences; there is no discard flag.
    • Version marker: template/.claude/skills/factory/VERSION holds X.Y.Z. The release PR must set it in the same commit that renames Unreleased to vX.Y.Z; a new version job in template CI compares it with the first - vX.Y.Z bullet here. Generated repos keep using .copier-answers.yml _commit.
    • Repos that adopted the skill by hand: the sync skill does not exist in your copy yet. Once, copy only template/.claude/skills/sync-root-factory from the new release tag (do not re-copy factory/: that would bring its VERSION and skip every hand-port), commit it so the tree is clean, then run the sync with --assume-tag <the tag your existing factory/ folder was copied from> (see "Adopt in an existing repo"). Releases before this one have no VERSION, so --assume-tag is needed that one time.
    • Template CI checks the new files in every render, runs sync.py --self-test (offline: temp dirs and local bare repos) and the VERSION check.
  • v0.7.0 (2026-11-25): Real-data access is a per-repo choice (#33, from pensieve-traces, which allows reading real data shapes), plus ready-to-merge follow-ups (#35).
  • The skill no longer hard-codes "agents may not read real user data".
  • Question: real_data_access (never, with-approval, allowed; default never, so copier update changes behaviour for no one). It renders a ## Real data section in CLAUDE.md whose first line is Real data: <level>..
  • Always on: never commit real data; never quote values from it (field names, counts and shapes only); tests use synthetic fixtures only; read data where it lives and never copy it into the repo or worktree; a stricter hard rule overrides the level.
  • with-approval: the maintainer approves one named source on the issue or PR, for that issue or PR only. Standing access means allowed.
  • Skill: "Reality check" reads the line from CLAUDE.md on main. A missing or unrecognised line means never. Briefs carry the rule to every subagent; reviewers tag real-data values in the diff or text as a blocker.
  • Repos that adopted the skill by hand (such as pensieve-traces) must add a Real data: <level>. line, or run copier update --data real_data_access=<level>; until then they read as never.
  • Template CI renders with-approval and allowed and guards the rendered text.
  • Ready-to-merge follow-ups (#35). The opt-in rule's docs say it matches only commands ending in --delete-branch. queue.py --json adds waiting_to_merge ([{"issue", "pr"}]) and the table lists a loose merge issue once. The skill names the stale-label check (gh issue list --state closed --label factory:ready-to-merge). docs/reference/scripts.md says issues, not PRs, carry the label.
  • v0.6.0 (2026-11-25): Two lessons from pensieve-traces. Docs ship with the code (#30), whose README still called a built feature "planned", and a ready-to-merge hand-off (#32), because Claude Code's auto mode refused the skill's --admin merge.
  • Docs ship with the code (#30).
  • Hard rule in CLAUDE.md, replacing "every user-visible change updates README.md and CHANGELOG.md": every code change ships its docs in the same PR, both new docs and updates to any README, CHANGELOG, docstring or .factory/designs/ text it makes wrong or stale. Docs that disagree with the PR's code break a hard rule, so they're a blocker even in mvp. Mismatches outside the PR's diff are filed, not fixed.
  • Documentation tech-debt issue: one open issue titled exactly "Documentation tech-debt" (documentation, P2) whose native sub-issues (documentation, improvement, P2) are the doc todos. bootstrap.sh creates it and the documentation label; the skill finds it by title and creates it if missing, so existing repos need no re-bootstrap. New lanes.py doc-debt find|add|list. queue.py never lists the tracking issue as work.
  • Skill: the builder updates the docs its change affects and adds a Docs line to the Handoff (docs updated, or "none needed" and why). The code reviewer checks docs against code in the changed area: a mismatch the PR causes is a blocker, an older one is the new doc-debt tag. The orchestrator files doc-debt findings as sub-issues of the tracking issue (not in the PR's improvement issue) and resolves their threads with the link. Ride-alongs: the builder gets the open doc todos and fixes those about files its PR already touches (Closes #N). Documentation todos from planning also go under the tracking issue.
  • New merge gate 12, "Docs ship with the code": the Handoff's Docs line is present, and a diff that changes code but no docs states a reason that holds up. "You aren't unsure" is now gate 13.
  • The issue format's "Docs updated" criterion names the specific docs, and there's a format for doc todos. The Actions-path build-from-design (a "## Docs" PR section) and review-against-design (a "Docs vs code" check) follow the same rule.
  • Fixed along the way: SKILL.md said "Three principles" above four.
  • Ready-to-merge hand-off (#32). When every gate passes but the merge is refused (the harness denies gh pr merge, or GitHub rejects it), that is no longer a dead end.
  • Skill: step 8 tries the merge; if it is refused, the skill never works around it (no gh api, other flags or other tools). It labels the PR and issue factory:ready-to-merge, posts one PR comment with the exact merge command and the gate summary, removes the in-progress label and moves on, like flag-and-continue. The end-of-run report lists these PRs so you can merge in one batch.
  • Merge command: plain gh pr merge <PR> --merge --delete-branch when mergeStateStatus is CLEAN; --admin only when the PR is blocked solely by the required review. Gate 2 no longer presents --admin as the only path.
  • queue.py: new state merge (uses no slot; the lane's later issues wait) and a "Waiting for you to merge" list. bootstrap.sh creates the factory:ready-to-merge label.
  • Opt-in: the generated README and the docs explain how to add a Claude Code permission rule for gh pr merge * --merge --admin --delete-branch so the skill can merge itself. The template ships no such rule, and the ruleset is unchanged.
  • Template CI guards check the new label, state, hand-off text and opt-in docs.
  • runlog.py status shows an issue whose last step is ready-to-merge as waiting on the maintainer, not in flight (#36).
  • v0.5.1 (2026-11-24): Data-loss blocker (#27). Reviewers now treat this as a blocker, not an improvement: irreversible loss or overwrite of the user's existing data (source files, history, remote repos) on a plausible invocation, even a mistaken one, when a cheap guard would prevent it. The design reviewer asks plans that write, move or delete files to name their overwrite rules. Updated in the Code and Design reviewer briefs, the review command, CLAUDE.md, the README and the pipeline docs.
  • v0.5.0 (2026-11-24): Swim lanes (#23). Work is organised as prioritized lanes of ordered, dependency-linked issues.
  • Lanes: a parent issue labelled lane whose native GitHub sub-issues are processed one at a time, in order. Priorities P0–P3 on lanes and issues. Dependencies between issues or whole lanes use native "blocked by" links, with the body's "Depends on #N" line kept as a fallback.
  • Brainstorm is two-level: lanes (priorities, lane dependencies, main path), then ordered issues per lane, with rolling-wave detail (only the next one or two issues fully written). One confirmation creates everything.
  • Scheduling: queue.py is lane-aware. Each lane's current issue and state, lanes ranked by priority, "Work now" for --lanes N. One lane at a time by default; the skill asks the maintainer before running more lanes in parallel. A question on a lane pauses only that lane. A collision guard holds a second lane whose plan touches the same files.
  • New scripts/lanes.py (sub-add, order, block, priority, project-add, show) wraps the GitHub sub-issue, dependency and Projects calls.
  • bootstrap.sh creates the lane and P0–P3 labels and a GitHub Project board with a Priority field (needs the project scope).
  • First real test: pensieve-traces restructured into four lanes.
  • v0.4.0 (2026-11-24): Flag and continue (#21). The skill never blocks the session waiting for the maintainer.
  • Questions (a reviewer's [question], a design reviewer's ASK, gate failures, unverifiable data assumptions, persistent blockers) are posted as inline, line-anchored PR review comments with options and a recommendation. The issue and PR get factory:needs-maintainer, and the run moves on to independent work. An in-session question only when nothing else can proceed.
  • Resume ("resume the factory") works from GitHub state: queue.py shows which waiting PRs have new maintainer replies. Answers are applied by Opus directly for small edits, or by a Sonnet resume builder otherwise. Then an Opus check scoped to those threads, then the gates. @claude on the PR (Actions factory-chat) also works.
  • Builder handoffs: the builder keeps a "## Handoff" section in the PR body after every phase. Replacement agents and reviewers start from it. At merge, its gist goes into .factory/designs/issue-N.md as "Implementation notes".
  • Where knowledge lives: GitHub and the repo are the source of truth; the run log is a local cache and cost ledger that only points at them; Claude's memory holds preferences. New CLAUDE.md section.
  • Gates: new "Handoff present" and "all review threads resolved". bootstrap.sh turns on "require conversation resolution" and creates the factory:needs-maintainer label. gates.md documents the API calls for posting inline questions and for finding and resolving threads.
  • The plan phase now opens a draft PR, so plan-level questions can be anchored to lines.
  • runlog.py schema v2: actor, refs (commit, thread ids), steps needs-maintainer, resume, handoff-written; cost by role. queue.py: needs-maintainer state, with replied first.
  • v0.3.1 (2026-11-24): Fix: the skill now works on local/issue-N branches, so the GitHub Actions factory-review (which watches factory/issue-*) no longer duplicates the skill's own Opus review on every push. The per-run "disable the Actions review?" question is removed, and template CI checks both. Fix: bootstrap.sh now creates the improvement label that the v0.3.0 skill depends on (template CI checks it). Docs: the README is rewritten for the skill-first workflow: both ways to run the factory (the factory skill and GitHub Actions), how the skill keeps cost down, the release_phase question, the skill and run-log files, using the skill in a repo not generated from the template, and how the template evolves (lessons → releases → copier update).
  • v0.3.0 (2026-11-24): A faster, cheaper factory skill, from running pensieve-traces #2 and #3 (about 1.4M subagent tokens for two issues).
  • Urgency triage (#17): a release_phase question (mvp by default) writes a "Release phase" section into CLAUDE.md. In mvp, reviewers tag findings blocker or improvement; only blockers are fixed in-PR; the orchestrator files one batched improvement issue per PR, and main-path issues never depend on improvements. queue.py lists ready main-path issues before ready improvements.
  • 2 subagents per issue instead of 10–15: one Sonnet builder plans (phase 1), builds (phase 2) and fixes blockers, each step a SendMessage to the same agent, so it never re-reads context (#14). One fresh Opus code reviewer runs in parallel with CI. Blocker fixes are verified by CI plus the orchestrator's repro, with no re-review. Risk tiers: only critical issues (privacy/security, new dependencies, shared data contracts) get a separate Opus design review. Standard issues get an orchestrator plan skim.
  • Run log (#14): scripts/runlog.py (add, status, summary) writes .factory/runs/*.jsonl (gitignored). Sessions resume an in-flight issue, and the end-of-run summary reports wall time, fix rounds and tokens by model. The skill suggests a fresh session after 2–3 issues.
  • Overlap (#15): plan an independent ready issue while another builds; at most two in flight; merges one at a time, updating the other branch with main afterwards.
  • Reality check (#13): never build on an unverifiable assumption about real data; ask the maintainer, ideally with a local shape-only script. The issue format records what was verified against real data, plus the risk tier.
  • Bounded CI waits: watch the workflow run (gh run watch <id>), not PR checks; no sleep loops. Rerun to clear a stale pending check.
  • Template CI checks all of the above, including the runlog.py self-test.
  • v0.2.0 (2026-11-24): factory skill: run the factory from a Claude Code session instead of label by label.
  • Brainstorm mode: Opus brainstorms with the maintainer, proposes an issue breakdown, gets one confirmation, Sonnet subagents draft Factory-task issues and Opus checks and creates them with dependency links.
  • Run mode: for each ready issue (scripts/queue.py, dependency-ordered), Sonnet designs → an Opus subagent reviews the design → Sonnet builds in a worktree → CI → a fresh Opus subagent reviews the code → Opus auto-merges (--merge --admin) when every gate in references/gates.md passes.
  • Stops and asks when unsure, on failed gates, or on workflow, dependency, version or CLAUDE.md changes. Never adds the Actions trigger labels, so the two modes don't duplicate work.
  • Template CI checks the skill files and runs queue.py --self-test.
  • Hardened by its first real run (pensieve-traces #2, #3), lessons #10, #11, #12 and #16: reviewers don't add unverifiable scope (it becomes a question); stop when two rounds find defects in the same area; narrow "Design final check" and "Code re-review" briefs; non-blocking notes and (optional) items (optional items are filed as linked follow-up issues); a Reviewer-notes slot in the Builder brief; repo slug taken from gh, not memory; a rule for installing outside packages; asks whether to disable the weaker Actions review for the run; design length cap by size (S ~400, M ~800 words); design-issue handles local-mode labels.
  • v0.1.1 (2026-11-24): Fixes from driving the first generated factory (pensieve-traces) end to end.
  • Build and chat agents can run checks on PRs authored by claude[bot] (restrict_untrusted_prs: "false"), protected by a new build step that refuses design branches touching anything outside .factory/designs/ (#3).
  • The review agent runs on implementation PRs opened by claude[bot] (allowed_bots: "claude") (#5), and verifies "Checks run" against CI with gh pr checks instead of trying to run code (#6).
  • The build agent reports denied or missing commands on the design PR with factory:blocked, never a silent exit (#3).
  • Docs: a "Changing the factory itself" section in the generated README. It covers workflow changes in their own PR (#7), updating open factory PRs after a workflow change (#4), merging your own PRs, and treating "green but no artifact" as a failure. CLAUDE.md and the build prompt say the same.
  • Template CI asserts every guardrail above is present in the rendered project.
  • v0.1.0 (2026-11-24): First release as a Copier template, generalized from pensieve-traces. Factory workflows, agent commands, issue template, CI, package skeleton, scripts/bootstrap.sh (labels, main ruleset, fork-PR approval), and a template CI that renders three variants and runs their checks.

docs.title: 47 (from the #45 review): the factory-lesson skill's duplicate search now covers closed lessons too (--state all). A closed match points to the release that fixed it and to updating (copier update, or sync-root-factory) instead of filing a duplicate. If you edit the draft at the confirmation step, the privacy check runs again on the edited text and its result is shown before filing. Template CI guards the new text.
42: the queue.py self-test asserts on the --json payload (now built by payload()); the skill's stale-label step also clears factory:ready-to-merge from merged PRs.
Merge gates
docs.text:
The orchestrator merges only when every gate holds on the PR's current commit. A reviewer's summary is evidence, not proof. If a gate fails and the fix isn't mechanical, the factory flags and continues.

# Gate How it's checked 1 CI green A run-level watch: every required check passes, none pending 2 Up to date with main mergeStateStatus isn't BEHIND or DIRTY; if behind, update the branch and re-check gate 1. BLOCKED alone means the merge needs your bypass or approval 3 No open blockers The review returned READY, or every blocker was fixed and verified with its reproduction 4 Deviations disclosed and minor The PR's "Deviations" section plus the reviewer's undisclosed deviations 5 No hard-rule violations The orchestrator's own read of the diff against CLAUDE.md 6 No workflow changes Nothing under .github/; those go to you, in their own PR 7 Dependency changes exactly as planned pyproject.toml matches the plan; uv.lock only follows 8 CLAUDE.md and .claude/ unchanged gh pr diff --name-only 9 Closes its issue Closes #N in the PR body 10 Handoff present An up-to-date ## Handoff section 11 All review threads resolved The GraphQL unresolved-thread query returns 0; also enforced by the ruleset 12 Docs ship with the code The Handoff has a Docs line naming the docs updated, or "none needed" with a reason; a diff that changes code but no docs needs that reason, and it must hold up 13 Not unsure The orchestrator skims the diff; if anything still bothers it, it asks instead of merging

Merges use merge commits, so release tags stay on main, and happen one at a time.

docs.title: The merge command
docs.text: mergeStateStatus Command CLEAN gh pr merge <PR> --merge --delete-branch BLOCKED only by the required review gh pr merge <PR> --merge --admin --delete-branch (your ruleset bypass)

docs.title: When the merge is refused
docs.text: If the harness denies the command or GitHub rejects it, the factory stops there. It never retries through gh api, other flags or another tool. Instead it labels the PR and issue factory:ready-to-merge, removes the in-progress label, posts one comment (Ready to merge: all gates pass on <sha>., the merge command that fits, the gate summary) and moves on. See Flag and continue.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
• Only you advance work. Every Actions trigger checks the sender is maintainer_github, and a label guard strips trigger labels anyone else adds. The skill runs in your session.
  • Forks can't run agents. Build, review and chat refuse PRs from forks, and fork-PR workflows need your approval.
  • Least privilege per stage. Reviewers can't push. The build step refuses design branches that touch anything outside .factory/designs/. Per-stage tool allowlists apply.
  • Merge gates (skill): see Merge gates.
  • Protected main. A ruleset: PRs with approval and code-owner review, all conversations resolved, required checks, no force push or deletion.
  • Bounded cost. timeout-minutes, --max-turns and per-issue concurrency on every Actions job; pinned models; urgency triage; the run log's cost report.
  • Hard rules in CLAUDE.md: no secrets or personal data, a per-repo real-data level (never by default; real data is never committed or quoted, tests use synthetic fixtures), no uploads, no paid model endpoints, dependencies only as planned, no version bumps or releases, no workflow changes unless planned (and then in their own PR).
  • You merge the factory itself. PRs touching .github/, CLAUDE.md or .claude/ are never merged by the skill.

The template CI renders three variants and fails if any of these is missing from a generated repo.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
Label Meaning Added by lane A parent issue whose sub-issues run in order the skill (brainstorm) P0 P1 P2 P3 Priority: now, next, later, someday the skill, you improvement Non-blocking finding, filed instead of fixed (mvp phase) the skill documentation The "Documentation tech-debt" tracking issue and its sub-issues (doc todos) bootstrap.sh, the skill factory:needs-maintainer A question waits for you on this PR the skill factory:ready-to-merge Every gate passed but the merge was refused: you merge it (the command is in the PR comment) the skill factory:design Actions mode: start the design agent you only design:approved Actions mode: start the build agent you only factory:designing, factory:building, factory:review Actions-mode progress workflows factory:blocked An agent stopped and needs you workflows, the skill lesson (amplifactory only) a factory problem found in a project you, the skill

The label guard removes factory:design and design:approved when anyone but you adds them, and the skill never adds them.

docs.title: Copier questions
docs.text:
Question Default Used for project_name — Repo and distribution name (kebab-case) package_name project_name with _ Python import name, package directory cli_name project_name Console script and starter cli.py; empty for a library description — pyproject, GitHub description, README tagline agent_context description What the project is, at the top of CLAUDE.md extra_hard_rules none Project-specific CLAUDE.md hard rules (one - bullet each) design_risks privacy/data, licensing, dependencies, docs What every plan's Risks section must cover issue_areas [core, cli, docs, tests, none] "Areas affected" dropdown in the issue template maintainer_github the template author The only login the workflows obey; CODEOWNERS author_name, author_email, homepage the template author's pyproject, README python_min, python_versions 3.11, ["3.11", "3.12"] requires-python, CI matrix, required checks ruff_version 0.17.4 Pinned ruff in CI, CLAUDE.md and the agents' tool allowlists release_phase mvp CLAUDE.md "Release phase": mvp fixes only blockers in-PR; hardening reviews thoroughly real_data_access never CLAUDE.md "Real data": never (you run shapes-only scripts), with-approval (agents ask per issue, then read locally) or allowed. Real data is never committed or quoted at any level agent_model sonnet --model for the Actions-mode agents (the skill picks its own models)

Answers are stored in .copier-answers.yml and reused by copier update. Change one with uvx copier update --data release_phase=hardening. The same works for real_data_access (uvx copier update --data real_data_access=<level>); make the change in its own PR. Editing CLAUDE.md by hand also works, but then .copier-answers.yml disagrees with it.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: The first three live in .claude/skills/factory/scripts/, need only Python ≥3.9 (macOS's system python3 works) and gh, and have a --self-test. sync.py (also Python ≥3.9) belongs to the sync-root-factory skill and is described at the end.

docs.title: queue.py
docs.text:
The lane-aware queue: what to work on now.

python .claude/skills/factory/scripts/queue.py              # table + "Work now"
python .claude/skills/factory/scripts/queue.py --lanes 2    # two lanes in parallel
python .claude/skills/factory/scripts/queue.py --json
Option Meaning --lanes N lanes in parallel (default 1) --json machine-readable output --offline skip the reply and dependency API calls --maintainer LOGIN whose replies count (default: the logged-in gh user)

Lane states, from the lane's current issue: active (a PR in progress), replied (you answered a question), merge (every gate passed but the merge was refused, so you merge it; uses no slot, and the lane's later issues wait), ready, asked (waiting on you; uses no slot), blocked, waiting (on another lane or issue), done.

Issues labelled factory:ready-to-merge are also listed under "Waiting for you to merge", each with its PR. A loose one appears only there, not under "Not in a lane". --json has the same list as waiting_to_merge: [{"issue": N, "pr": M}] (pr is null when no open PR is found).

The "Documentation tech-debt" tracking issue is never listed as work; its open sub-issues appear under "Not in a lane" as improvements.

docs.title: lanes.py
docs.text:
Creates and maintains lanes with native GitHub features. The sub-issue and dependency APIs need internal issue ids; lanes.py looks them up.

Command Does sub-add LANE ISSUE… append issues to the end of a lane, in this order (keeps the existing order; skips ones already there) order LANE ISSUE… move these issues to the front, in this order (sub-add never does this) block ISSUE --by ISSUE… add "blocked by" links (safe to re-run) priority ISSUE P0…P3 set exactly one priority label project-add ISSUE… --project N add to the Project board and set its Priority field from the label show LANE print the lane's order doc-debt find print the "Documentation tech-debt" issue's number, creating it (and its labels) if missing doc-debt add --title T --body-file F file a doc todo (documentation, improvement, P2) as a sub-issue of it doc-debt add --issue N label an existing issue as a doc todo and link it as a sub-issue doc-debt list [--json] the open doc todos, which the builder gets for ride-alongs

The tracking issue is found by its exact title, open and labelled documentation; if there are several, the oldest wins.

docs.title: runlog.py
docs.text:
The run log in .factory/runs/<date>.jsonl: a local cache and cost ledger that points at GitHub.

python .claude/skills/factory/scripts/runlog.py add --issue 4 --step plan --actor builder \
    --model sonnet --tokens 41000 --ms 52000 --pr 29 --note "plan pushed"
python .claude/skills/factory/scripts/runlog.py status     # last step per issue
python .claude/skills/factory/scripts/runlog.py summary    # wall time, rounds, tokens by model

Steps: plan, plan-check, design-review, build, review, fix, handoff-written, needs-maintainer, resume, merge, ready-to-merge, blocked, decision, improvement-filed.

docs.title: sync.py
docs.text:
The guards of the sync-root-factory skill (.claude/skills/sync-root-factory/scripts/). It needs git, and gh only for labels. Run the target tag's copy, extracted outside the repo, with --repo <repo root> (see the adopt guide), not the one in the repo. Every command that refuses prints refused: <why>, exits 1. Each refuses before writing, with two exceptions that say so: apply's post-write diff (undo with git restore . and git clean -fd on the folders it names) and labels --create, which reports the labels created before a failure.

# sf = python3 -I "$T/x/template/.claude/skills/sync-root-factory/scripts/sync.py" --repo "$R"
# (the target tag's copy, extracted outside the repo: see the adopt guide)
sf preflight
sf status [--assume-tag vX.Y.Z]
sf branch vX.Y.Z
sf verify-local [--assume-tag vX.Y.Z]
sf apply --to-tag vX.Y.Z [--assume-tag vX.Y.Z]
sf copier-check vX.Y.Z
Command What it does preflight refuses inside amplifactory or on a dirty tree (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all not empty); prints generated or shadowing latest the highest vX.Y.Z tag of the template status current version (_commit, or factory/VERSION), latest tag and behind / up-to-date; refuses a downgrade or a non-tag _commit branch TAG creates local/adopt-TAG from a fresh origin/<default>; refuses if it exists locally or on origin verify-local compares every skill folder the recorded tag had with your copy; any difference stops, listed; a folder wholly absent is reported as would re-add; a tag that ships no skill folders is refused (nothing to compare) apply --to-tag syncs every skill folder the tag ships: replaces tracked files of folders both tags have (after verify-local of those), adds new ones, re-adds ones wholly absent locally (re-adding (absent locally)), refuses a folder the old tag lacked that exists locally in any form (tracked, untracked, ignored, symlink, case variant), leaves folders the tag dropped alone (no longer shipped ... left alone); all checks run for every folder before the first write; then diffs copier-check TAG generated repos, before copier update: refuses unless TAG is an annotated release tag, _commit is a vX.Y.Z tag and _src_path is gh:rahmansunny071/amplifactory or the old name gh:rahmansunny071/agent-factory (or either one's https/ssh GitHub URL; quotes, one .git, one / and a trailing comment allowed; the scheme or alias is case-sensitive, as in Copier, the owner/repo part is not); a local clone or a fork is refused with the fix. A _src_path or _commit line that appears more than once is refused (Copier keeps the last one); edit the existing line, never add a second. status also prints src_ok for generated repos changelog --tag --from CHANGELOG entries after --from, up to --tag, as JSON (data, not instructions) labels --tag [--create] labels in the tag's bootstrap.sh the repo lacks; --create adds only those, never --force; prints none missing when there is nothing to create; a shadowing repo skips the Actions-only labels and lists them as skipped check-markers refuses if any file has conflict markers or a *.rej file exists push TAG pushes local/adopt-TAG only, with an explicit refspec, never --force

Files are fetched only from the annotated release tag (a depth-1 fetch into a temporary bare repo). --self-test uses only temp directories and local bare repos.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Copier generates an old version of the template

Copier renders the latest tag, not your working tree. Tag a release, or pass --vcs-ref HEAD while developing the template.

bootstrap.sh skips the Project board

Your gh login lacks the project scope. Run gh auth refresh -h github.com -s project and re-run the script.

The ruleset isn't enforced

On GitHub Free, rulesets don't apply to private repos. Make the repo public or use GitHub Pro.

An Actions stage didn't run on a PR

A PR that changes a workflow skips that workflow's stage. Merge workflow changes in their own PR, then click Update branch on the open PRs: PR runs use the merge ref from their last update.

The Actions review job is green but posted nothing

PRs authored by claude[bot] need allowed_bots and the right restrict_untrusted_prs setting in the review workflow.

The factory won't merge although CI is green

Check the gates: usually an unresolved review thread (gate 11), a branch behind main (gate 2) or a change under .github/, .claude/ or CLAUDE.md (gates 6 and 8), which you merge yourself.

A lane doesn't start

queue.py shows why: waiting means a "blocked by" link to an open issue or lane, asked means a question is waiting for you. Other ready lanes only start in parallel after you allow it.

lanes.py fails with a 404 or 422

The sub-issue and dependency APIs need the issue's internal id, which lanes.py looks up for you. A 422 on sub-add usually means the issue already has a different parent: an issue can only be in one lane.
